transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-09
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Connor (Redwood Product); Aisha (HelioCloud PM), Tom (HelioCloud Cloud Eng), Rita (HelioCloud Solutions), Samir (HelioCloud Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements and the reference architecture for Redwood's runtime on HelioCloud, identify security gaps and next steps for a joint solution listing.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're on for about 45, 50 minutes, um quick intros. i'm maya, i'm the AE on the partnership, luca is our se, conor product will jump in.
[00:12] Aisha: hi everyone, aisha here, marketplace product manager at heliocloud, we also have tom and rita and samir on the call.
[00:20] Luca: great, thanks. agenda — marketplace listing requirements, reference arch, packaging, security questions, and timeline. sound OK?
[00:28] Tom: yes, that works. we want to understand how to package the redwood runtime so it can be a one-click deploy in our marketplace and also how billing and metering would work.
[00:39] Maya: perfect. so high level, Redwood supports hosted api, dedicated and private deployments — for marketplace we usually do a container-backed offering with a terraform module and helm chart for customers to deploy into their account, or we offer a managed listing where we host. which model are you targeting?
[00:53] Aisha: our product team prefers a marketplace listing that allows customers to deploy into their own account (bring-your-own infra) but for some enterprise customers we want an option to offer a managed deployment. so both, ideally.
[01:05] Rita: one question up front — does redwood provide a reference arch for vpc peering / private deployments? our security team will want to know about network isolation and kms integration.
[01:13] Luca: yes, we have a reference architecture that shows VPC options, private control plane patterns, and KMS/HSM integrations. typically we provide a terraform module that sets up the networking primitives and an optional vpn / transit gateway pattern for private control plane. we can share that.
[01:29] Samir: when you say KMS/HSM integration, does that require a specific KMS provider or can we use our HSM-backed keys?
[01:36] Connor: we support standard cloud KMS providers out of the box and we also have a path for HSM via customer-managed key material — it's more of an enterprise setup and we have documentation. there may be additional attestation steps for HSM.
[01:48] Tom: for the terraform/helm, do you publish modules on terraform registry / helm repo or do you expect partners to host artifacts?
[01:56] Maya: we publish reference modules in a public repo and can publish to terraform registry on request; for helm charts we have a stable release tarball and partner-specific values files. partners often mirror the chart in their marketplace artifact repo.
[02:09] Aisha: good to know. what about licensing and eula text for the marketplace? we need a standard set of assets and also a logo pack.
[02:17] Maya: yes we have a marketplace asset pack — logos, eula, support SLAs, and a standard listing description. we'll share a zip in the checklist.
[02:25] [02:25] Rita: ok. on security, our compliance team is asking for SOC2 report and pen test summary, can you share those?
[02:33] Luca: yes, we can provide SOC2 type II report and recent pen test summary under an NDA; we'll add that to the onboarding artifacts.
[02:41] Samir: also curious about audit logs and telemetry — we'd prefer logs flow into our centralized log collector, and we need to know retention controls.
[02:49] Luca: the runtime emits audit logs and tracing that can be forwarded via our connectors (s3, syslog, datadog). retention is configurable in the deployment manifest; for managed listing we retain per contract.
[03:02] Aisha: going back to billing — how does marketplace usage metering map to redwood usage? token counting? per-hour capacity?
[03:11] Connor: typically marketplace billings are either a subscription for reserved capacity (dedicated) or metered per-token for hosted. for the BYO deploy pattern we can include a billing connector that reports usage via a metering endpoint back to Redwood for consolidated billing with the marketplace.
[03:26] Tom: can you elaborate on metering endpoint — is it push-based or pull-based, and is there an API spec?
[03:32] Luca: it's push-based — the deployment includes a small agent that aggregates usage at the virtual host and posts to our meter API. we publish an OpenAPI spec and sample payloads.
[03:44] Aisha: great. any limitations around model sizes or instance types? our marketplace has a set of allowed instance families.
[03:52] Maya: we support various model sizes; the reference arch includes recommended instance types for different model classes (e.g., 1-2x A100 equivalents for enterprise LLMs, T4/RTX for smaller). we'll include notes for quantized variants.
[04:07] Rita: can you confirm whether kv cache or prefix caching requires sticky sessions or stateful storage? this affects whether we can autoscale.
[04:16] Luca: good question — the KV cache and long context optimizations are managed in-memory per runtime; for scale-out we use a sharded cache or optional external KV that you can provide. we'll outline the autoscaling guidance.
[04:29] Samir: are there any native ingress controls for per-tenant RBAC? we need to enforce RBAC via SSO (SAML) and tie to our identity provider.
[04:38] Connor: yes, we support SAML/SSO and can map roles. for BYO deployments you can integrate with your IdP; for managed listings we can perform an SSO integration per customer.
[04:49] Maya: i'm going to share our marketplace checklist that covers all of this — artifacts, security, packaging, billing, and the sample terraform module.
[04:57] Aisha: perfect. maybe walk through the reference arch quick?
[05:04] Luca: sure — slide-free verbal: the ref arch has three main pieces: control plane (can be hosted or private), runtime nodes (gpu clusters in customer VPC), and ingress & observability layer. networking uses VPC endpoints or peering; KMS is used for key material; metrics are forwarded to partner telemetry. for marketplace we provide a terraform module that provisions the runtime autoscaling group, load balancers, and an optional node pool.
[05:29] Tom: for private control plane, how is the configuration pushed? do you use a webhook or an agent?
[05:35] Luca: configuration synchronization uses a small controller that runs in the customer cluster and polls the control plane via mutual TLS; for private control plane we use a connector that establishes a secure bi-directional channel. sometimes customers prefer a pull model only.
[05:48] Rita: do you have a published latency profile? product teams will want to set expectations.
[05:53] Maya: yes, we publish benchmarks for p50/p95 token latency per model and instance class. we'll include the performance deck in the package.
[06:02] Aisha: regarding the marketplace UX, we need a demo account and a quickstart so potential buyers can click to deploy and see a hello-world. do you have a sandbox image?
[06:11] Connor: we do. we'll provide a lightweight sandbox container with a small model and preconfigured values so the click-to-deploy experience is quick.
[06:19] Tom: on the operator side, what's involved in upgrades? in the marketplace we need clear upgrade path so customers can patch.
[06:26] Luca: we support rolling upgrades through helm with image tags; for critical CVEs we provide urgent patch docs and recommended replacement images. the terraform module supports blue/green or canary patterns.
[06:38] Samir: for compliance we need to know data residency controls — if a customer deploys in eu-west can you guarantee that control plane artifacts (logs, traces) won't leave region?
[06:48] Connor: yes, we have region-pin options; the private control plane pattern ensures logs and key material stay in region. managed options are contract-specific.
[06:58] Aisha: ok sounds good. one thing from legal: we need a standard support SLA for marketplace listings, can you confirm standard response times?
[07:06] Maya: our partner marketplace SLA is usually business-hour standard support, with an optional premium support add-on for 24/7 and faster RTOs. we can provide the SLA doc.
[07:14] Tom: in terms of manifest, can you share an example marketplace manifest that includes pricing fields and deployment variables?
[07:22] Maya: yes, we'll send a sample manifest. typically it includes pricing tiers (per-token, reserved), install variables, instance type selectors, and permission scopes.
[07:31] Aisha: from a Helio perspective, our marketplace requires a security questionnaire to be filled for each vendor. can you fill it?
[07:37] Luca: yes we'll fill it; we may need an NDA for some doc exchange but we can fill the standard questionnaire.
[07:44] Rita: technical nit — do you support cloud-native autoscaling (keda) or do you rely on cluster autoscaler?
[07:51] Luca: both — we have a KEDA scaler for event-driven patterns and recommend cluster autoscaler for GPU node pools combined with our internal autoscaler.
[08:01] Maya: sounds like we've covered most of the infra topics. let's talk packaging for the joint solution listing — marketing collateral, reference-arch doc, a joint whitepaper?
[08:11] Aisha: yes marketing would like a one-pager, a how-it-works diagram, and a joint case study if possible. we'll coordinate on copy.
[08:20] Connor: Redwood can draft a technical reference-arch and a short whitepaper; HelioCloud can contribute deployment numbers once we do a pilot.
[08:29] Tom: pilot — what's the proposed scope? minimal: deploy the ref arch into a heliocloud sandbox, run a standard workload (1M tokens) and report performance and cost.
[08:40] Maya: that sounds good. we'll propose a pilot plan in the follow up email.
[08:46] Samir: any security blockers we should know about — firewall exceptions, outbound ports, etc?
[08:51] Luca: runtime needs outbound to the meter endpoint and control plane on secure ports; we can provide a minimal ports list.
[08:59] Aisha: perfect. ok next steps recap?
[09:04] Maya: recap: i'll share marketplace checklist + asset pack, luca will upload sample terraform module and helm chart, conor will add performance deck, rita will confirm infra constraints, samir will send compliance matrix. we'll schedule follow-up for 2027-05-20 to review manifest.
[09:20] Tom: thanks everyone.
[09:22] Maya: thanks all. end.

Notes: Transcription includes occasional mis-heard words; speaker labels approximate. Attachments referenced: marketplace_checklist_v1.zip (to be shared), ref-arch-terraform-module.tar.gz (to be shared), performance-deck.pdf (to be shared).
